slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 12:3: I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you; and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you.
slides.body: “I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you; and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you.”
slides.heading: Gen 12:3

slides.alt_text: Slide one introduces the claim that Genesis 12:3 predicts worldwide blessing through Jesus.
slides.body: God tells Abraham that every family of the earth will be blessed through him. Galatians calls this advance gospel, and Christians identify Jesus as the descendant who brings that blessing.
slides.heading: Does Genesis promise Jesus will bless the nations?

slides.alt_text: Slide two presents the Christian canonical connection between the Abrahamic promise and Jesus.
slides.body: Genesis develops one promise: worldwide blessing through Abraham and later through his offspring. Galatians explicitly says Christ brings Abraham's blessing to the Gentiles by faith. Acts applies the offspring promise to God's raised servant.
slides.heading: The strongest Christian case

slides.alt_text: Slide three distinguishes Genesis's broad promise from the New Testament's specific christological reading.
slides.body: Genesis 12:3 says ‘through you’—Abraham—not ‘through your offspring.’ It promises worldwide blessing but never defines it as faith in Jesus. Galatians makes that later Christian interpretation explicit; Acts draws its offspring wording most directly from Genesis 22:18.
slides.heading: Explicit rereading, not an explicit name

title: Does Genesis promise Jesus will bless every nation?
